{
  "findings": [
    {
      "title": "Primary endpoint uses central review but secondary endpoints include investigator review, potential inconsistency",
      "quote": "The primary efficacy endpoint for this study is the ORR as determined by central review.",
      "page": 34,
      "section": "4.2.1",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "The primary endpoint is central review, but secondary endpoints include investigator review. This dual assessment may lead to discrepancies and complicate interpretation, but it is not a major flaw.",
      "fix": "Clarify how discrepancies between central and investigator review will be handled in the analysis."
    },
    {
      "title": "Inclusion criterion for HHI intolerance is overly complex and may be ambiguous",
      "quote": "Intolerance of prior HHI therapy defined as: (i) any Grade 3 or 4 AE deemed related to HHI (ii) Or any of the following HHI-related events in patients with at least 3 months of exposure to HHI therapy (exclusive of treatment breaks): • Grade 2 muscle spasms or myalgias (iia) • Grade 2 dysgeusia or anorexia, if accompanied by ≥Grade 1 weight loss (iib) • Grade 2 nausea or diarrhea despite medical management or (iic)",
      "page": 39,
      "section": "6.2.1",
      "category": "amendment_risk",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The definition of intolerance is highly specific and may be difficult to apply consistently across sites, leading to enrollment delays and potential amendments.",
      "fix": "Simplify the intolerance criteria or provide clearer guidance and examples."
    },
    {
      "title": "Inclusion criterion for 'no better than stable disease after 9 months' may be ambiguous",
      "quote": "No better than a stable disease after 9 months on HHI therapy (exclusive of treatment breaks)",
      "page": 39,
      "section": "6.2.1",
      "category": "amendment_risk",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The definition of 'no better than stable disease' is not specified (e.g., based on what criteria? RECIST? clinical?). This ambiguity could lead to inconsistent enrollment and amendments.",
      "fix": "Specify the criteria used to define stable disease (e.g., RECIST 1.1 or clinical criteria) and the timing of assessment."
    },
    {
      "title": "Safety monitoring for immune-related adverse events may be insufficient for anti-PD-1 therapy",
      "quote": "Assess the safety and tolerability of cemiplimab",
      "page": 31,
      "section": "2.2",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "Cemiplimab is an anti-PD-1 antibody, and immune-related adverse events (irAEs) are common. The protocol does not explicitly mention monitoring for irAEs (e.g., colitis, pneumonitis, hepatitis, endocrinopathies) in the safety assessments.",
      "fix": "Add specific monitoring and management guidelines for immune-related adverse events."
    },
    {
      "title": "Exploratory objectives require mandatory biopsies, which may be burdensome and lead to dropout",
      "quote": "Patients must consent to undergo biopsies of externally visible BCC lesions at baseline, cycle 1 day 22 (±3 business days), at time of tumor progression, and at other time points that may be clinically indicated",
      "page": 40,
      "section": "6.2.1",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "Mandatory on-treatment and progression biopsies are invasive and may cause patient discomfort, leading to poor compliance and potential selection bias.",
      "fix": "Consider making on-treatment biopsies optional or provide additional patient support."
    },
    {
      "title": "Inclusion criterion for Group 2 requires surgeon and radiation oncologist notes, which may delay enrollment",
      "quote": "A copy of the surgeon’s consultation note (surgeon may be site PI) from a clinical visit within 60 days of enrollment must be submitted.",
      "page": 40,
      "section": "6.2.1",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "Requiring a surgeon's note and a radiation oncologist's note (or multidisciplinary team note) within 60 days may be logistically challenging and delay enrollment, especially if specialists are not readily available.",
      "fix": "Allow a longer window for these notes or permit telemedicine consultations."
    },
    {
      "title": "Primary endpoint for Group 1 allows clinical response criteria for some patients, which may reduce objectivity",
      "quote": "Clinical response criteria may be used for patients with externally visible target lesions, if all metastatic lesions are not measurable by RECIST (such as may occur in patients with bone-only metastases).",
      "page": 34,
      "section": "4.2.1",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "Using different response criteria (RECIST vs. clinical) within the same group could lead to heterogeneity in the primary endpoint assessment and complicate interpretation.",
      "fix": "Clearly define how these patients will be analyzed and whether they will be pooled with RECIST-evaluable patients."
    },
    {
      "title": "Inclusion criterion for hepatic function is complex and may be difficult to implement",
      "quote": "Note for patients with hepatic metastases who wish to enroll in Group 1: If transaminase levels (AST and/or ALT) are >3x but ≤5x ULN, total bilirubin must be ≤1.5x ULN. If total bilirubin is >1.5x but ≤3x ULN, both transaminases (AST and ALT) must be ≤3x ULN.",
      "page": 40,
      "section": "6.2.1",
      "category": "amendment_risk",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "The hepatic function criteria are complex and may be misinterpreted, leading to enrollment errors and potential amendments.",
      "fix": "Simplify the criteria or provide a decision tree for investigators."
    }
  ]
}
